The amount of security is decided by the court itself as it is a discretion of the court. No one except the court before which the bail is pending has power to decide the amount of security to be paid. No, the amount is not refundable till the finality of the case. If the person who is accused of the offence gets acquitted, can file the application to get that security amount. Please note that if someone is intentionally refusing to return your money due to a valid reason like financial insolvency, it may be considered a civil dispute rather than a criminal one.

However, if there's evidence of **criminal breach of trust**, such as:

* Misappropriation of funds
* Theft or extortion involved in the non-return of money
* Any form of undue advantage taken by the person not returning your money

question: Sir I have purchased house from builders. Some dues of late fees in paying demand has been waived off by him as there was genuine problems but after registry when I email regarding some seepage issues he irritated and ask for pending dues.
ground_truth: A builder cannot ask for any payment post-registration of property in favour of the purchaser because it is a settled position and presumption of law that unless the seller/Builder gets full consideration value from the purchaser, he cannot execute a deed of conveyance in favour of the purchaser. As per Sub-Section 3 of Section 14 of the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016, In case any structural defect or any other defect in workmanship, quality or provision of services or any other obligations of the promoter as per the agreement for sale relating to such development is brought to the notice of the promoter within a period of five years by the allottee from the date of handing over possession, it shall be the duty of the promoter to rectify such defects without further charge, within thirty days, and in the event of the promoter's failure to rectify such defects within such time, the aggrieved allottees shall be entitled to receive appropriate compensation in the manner as provided under this Act. Being the above proposition of relevant law, if the housing complex is a registered project of RERA, then serving a legal notice to the Builder, file a complaint against the builder under Sec.31 of the Real Estate (Regulatory and Development) Act, 2016 before the Adjudicating Officer claiming compensation for the deficiency in service and breach of the Sub-Section 3 of Section 14 of the Act. Or else you can file a complaint against the Builder for deficiency in service and unfair trade practice before the Dist. Consumer Commission under Sec.35 of the Consumer Compensation Act, 2019 claiming compensation for harassment and cost of litigation. The complaint before the Consumer Court should be filed within two years from the date of the cause of action, It may be noted that you cannot raise your complaint/claim simultaneously before the Consumer Court and RERA for the same cause of action at a time.

Therefore, I would say that the proceedings against the builder, if initiated, might not reveal a commission of alleged criminal offense under section 420 IPC. Hence, it's likely that the court would quash the proceeding as it appears to be essentially civil in nature.
